whyThisShow: This is a canonical May '77 show, included in the official May 1977 box set release. One listener called it a "full-on, colossal '77 killer" while noting that "nearly everything the dead touched in may '77 turned to shimmering gold, but this show somehow grabbed me as being extra special". The second set is the gravitational center — one reviewer wrote that "the second set is where they absolutely bring the fucking hammer down though... every song is completely shit-hot". The Estimated Prophet > Eyes of the World sequence draws the most heat, with one listener saying "the ideas flowing out of Jerry's brain during this 25min segment is unparalled". The St. Stephen > Iko Iko > Not Fade Away closing sequence is described as "absolutely stunning" by another reviewer.
listenFor: In Estimated Prophet, Garcia deploys full wah, and one reviewer noted he gets "an incredibly rich, full sound" with an inside solo that "grew and prospered" as the band developed the song. In Eyes of the World, watch for Garcia's break before the "Redeemer" verse — he "ends a line with a brush of a chord; pauses; and then unleashes a beautiful run". One reviewer also flagged the Not Fade Away transition as "a marvelous transition, leaving the crowd wondering where they could possibly be going next". On the recording itself, one listener noted that "the first 3 or 4 songs the levels are a bit off.. (low) but that's at the source" before the board settles in. The Dancin' in the Streets has drawn particular attention, with one reviewer saying it is "one of the best of all-time".
context: This show falls squarely in the era-peak May 1977 run and was officially released as part of the May 1977 box set, giving it the band organization's own stamp. The best circulating recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd77-05-15.sbd.gorinsky.7008.sbeok.shnf), which has 92 reviews on Archive.org. One reviewer noted some hiss on the upload, speculating it was either tape hiss or cymbals not coming through quite right, and suggested "the tape I've had for years is much better (less hiss) than this upload". The St. Louis Arena setlist includes a rare first-set Scarlet > Fire pairing and an Iko Iko in the second set, which one reviewer flagged as "complete icing".
funFact: One reviewer noted that the show closes with what he called "probably the best reading" of Uncle John's Band he had ever heard, describing it as a must-hear encore.
headline: St. Louis, May '77 — the hammer comes down.
